paragraphs.title: Tension with Laban’s sons and the command to return

easy.question: What did Laban’s sons say about Jacob?
answers: Jacob took everything their father owned
Jacob returned to his ancestors’ land
Jacob helped their father
easy.explanation: Laban’s sons said that Jacob had taken everything their father owned.

easy.question: How did Laban feel toward Jacob compared with before?
answers: He was happier
He was no longer favorably disposed toward him
He did not recognize him
easy.explanation: Jacob saw that Laban’s attitude toward him had changed.

easy.question: What did the Lord command Jacob to do?
answers: Stay at Laban’s house
Take all of Laban’s property
Return to his fathers’ land and his relatives
easy.explanation: The Lord told Jacob to return to the land of his fathers and his relatives.

medium.question: Why did Jacob realize that Laban’s attitude had changed?
answers: He heard Laban’s sons and saw Laban’s expression
Rachel and Leah left him
The Lord told him Laban was angry
medium.explanation: Jacob heard Laban’s sons’ accusations and saw that Laban was no longer friendly toward him.

medium.question: In “Return unto the land of thy fathers, and to thy kindred,” what does “kindred” mean?
answers: Your father’s property
Your family or relatives
The road to Laban’s house
medium.explanation: “Kindred” means family or relatives, referring to Jacob’s people and homeland.

medium.question: What is the correct order of events?
answers: The Lord commanded Jacob, then Laban’s sons spoke, and finally Jacob saw Laban
Jacob saw Laban, then the Lord commanded him, and finally Laban’s sons spoke
Laban’s sons spoke, Jacob saw Laban, and then the Lord commanded him to return
medium.explanation: First Laban’s sons spoke, then Jacob saw Laban’s changed attitude, and finally the Lord commanded him to return.

challenge.question: What can be inferred from the Lord’s promise, “I will be with thee”?
answers: The Lord promised to guide and protect Jacob
The Lord promised Jacob would stay with Laban
The Lord promised Laban would give Jacob more property
challenge.explanation: The promise follows the command to return, expressing the Lord’s support and protection on Jacob’s journey.

challenge.question: What change in Laban’s attitude is described?
answers: Laban became richer
Laban no longer treated Jacob as he had before
Laban left his family
challenge.explanation: Laban was no longer favorably disposed toward Jacob as he had been before.

challenge.question: Why does the command to return come after the description of Laban’s attitude?
answers: To show that Jacob forgot his family
To explain that Laban asked Jacob to stay
To show that the tension with Laban formed part of the background to Jacob’s departure
challenge.explanation: Laban’s changed attitude helps explain the background and timing of Jacob’s departure.

questions.question: What can be inferred from the Lord’s promise, “I will be with thee”?
answers: The Lord promised to guide and protect Jacob
The Lord promised Jacob would stay with Laban
The Lord promised Laban would give Jacob more property
questions.explanation: The promise expresses the Lord’s support and protection on Jacob’s journey.

questions.question: What change in Laban’s attitude is described?
answers: Laban became richer
Laban no longer treated Jacob as he had before
Laban left his family
questions.explanation: Laban was no longer favorably disposed toward Jacob as he had been before.

questions.question: Why does the command to return come after the description of Laban’s attitude?
answers: To show that Jacob forgot his family
To explain that Laban asked Jacob to stay
To show that the tension with Laban formed part of the background to Jacob’s departure
questions.explanation: Laban’s changed attitude helps explain the background and timing of Jacob’s departure.

paragraphs.title: Jacob tells his wives about his work and success

easy.question: Whom did Jacob send for?
answers: Rachel and Leah
Laban and his sons
His servants
easy.explanation: Jacob sent for Rachel and Leah, his wives.

easy.question: Where did Jacob call Rachel and Leah?
answers: At Laban’s house
In the field with his flock
In the city
easy.explanation: Jacob called them in the field, near his flock.

easy.question: How did Jacob say he had served their father?
answers: Unwillingly
Very little
With all his strength
easy.explanation: Jacob reminded them that he had served their father with all his strength.

medium.question: What made Jacob realize that Laban’s attitude had changed?
answers: He saw that Laban’s expression was no longer favorable
Rachel and Leah asked him to leave
Laban’s flock disappeared
medium.explanation: Jacob saw that Laban’s attitude toward him was no longer as it had been.

medium.question: In “your father hath deceived me,” what does “deceived” mean?
answers: Helped me
Cheated or misled me
Praised me
medium.explanation: Laban repeatedly changed Jacob’s wages, so “deceived” means cheated or misled.

medium.question: What was the relationship between Laban’s changes to Jacob’s wages and Jacob’s success?
answers: Laban stopped changing the wages
Jacob gave up his wages
Despite the changes, God caused the wealth to pass to Jacob
medium.explanation: Although Laban changed Jacob’s wages, God prevented him from harming Jacob and gave Jacob the increase.

challenge.question: What can be inferred from Jacob’s words, “the God of my father hath been with me”?
answers: Jacob saw his success as also resulting from God’s care
Jacob claimed that Isaac was physically with him
Jacob asked Laban to work for him
challenge.explanation: Jacob emphasized that God had been with him and had protected and blessed him.

challenge.question: In “as before,” what time does Jacob refer to?
answers: The recent past
Only after three days
Since the birth of the sons
challenge.explanation: The phrase refers to the way things had been previously.

challenge.question: Which detail shows that Laban tried to control what kind of flock Jacob would receive?
answers: Jacob called Rachel and Leah in the field
Laban declared whether the wages would be speckled or ringstraked
God was with Jacob
challenge.explanation: Laban changed the wage conditions by specifying which markings the animals would have.

questions.question: What can be inferred from Jacob’s words, “the God of my father hath been with me”?
answers: Jacob saw his success as also resulting from God’s care
Jacob claimed that Isaac was physically with him
Jacob asked Laban to work for him
questions.explanation: Jacob emphasized that God had been with him and had protected and blessed him.

questions.question: In “as before,” what time does Jacob refer to?
answers: The recent past
Only after three days
Since the birth of the sons
questions.explanation: The phrase refers to the way things had been previously.

questions.question: Which detail shows that Laban tried to control what kind of flock Jacob would receive?
answers: Jacob called Rachel and Leah in the field
Laban declared whether the wages would be speckled or ringstraked
God was with Jacob
questions.explanation: Laban changed the wage conditions by specifying which markings the animals would have.

paragraphs.title: The dream and God’s message to Jacob

easy.question: What did Jacob see in his dream?
answers: Rams that were ringstraked, speckled, and grisled
Angels ascending a ladder
His sons returning to the land
easy.explanation: Jacob saw rams marked as ringstraked, speckled, and grisled.

easy.question: Who spoke to Jacob in the dream?
answers: Laban
The angel of God
Esau
easy.explanation: The angel of God spoke to Jacob in the dream.

easy.question: What did God command Jacob to do?
answers: Stay with Laban
Take all the flock
Leave the land and return to his relatives
easy.explanation: Jacob was told to leave the land and return to the land of his relatives.

medium.question: Why did the angel tell Jacob to look at the rams?
answers: Because God had seen everything Laban had done to Jacob
Because Jacob did not know the flock
Because Laban asked Jacob to count them
medium.explanation: The vision showed that God had seen the wrong Laban had done to Jacob.

medium.question: What is the correct order of events?
answers: Jacob left for his homeland and then had the dream
Jacob had the dream, the angel spoke, and then commanded him to return
Laban spoke to Jacob and then the angel appeared
medium.explanation: Jacob first saw the animals in a dream, then the angel explained the vision and commanded him to return.

medium.question: In “the rams which leap upon the cattle,” what are “rams”?
answers: Young sheep
Shepherds
Male sheep
medium.explanation: Rams are male sheep.

challenge.question: What central idea is expressed when the angel says, “I have seen all that Laban doeth unto thee”?
answers: God sees the wrong done to Jacob and watches over him
Laban is the fairest owner of the flock
Jacob’s dream had nothing to do with his life
challenge.explanation: The vision is connected to Laban’s actions and emphasizes God’s awareness and care.

challenge.question: Why does God mention Bethel and Jacob’s vow there?
answers: To remind Jacob of his work for Laban
To connect the command to return with an earlier vow and promise
To identify Laban’s home
challenge.explanation: The reference recalls Jacob’s earlier relationship with God and strengthens the command to return.

challenge.question: What does the repeated instruction to “lift up thine eyes” emphasize?
answers: The angel wanted Jacob to close his eyes
The event happened during the day, not in a dream
Jacob was to observe the vision carefully and understand its meaning
challenge.explanation: The repetition highlights Jacob’s attention to the vision and its significance.

questions.question: What central idea is expressed when the angel says, “I have seen all that Laban doeth unto thee”?
answers: God sees the wrong done to Jacob and watches over him
Laban is the fairest owner of the flock
Jacob’s dream had nothing to do with his life
questions.explanation: The vision emphasizes God’s awareness of Laban’s actions and care for Jacob.

questions.question: Why does God mention Bethel and Jacob’s vow there?
answers: To remind Jacob of his work for Laban
To connect the command to return with an earlier vow and promise
To identify Laban’s home
questions.explanation: The reference recalls Jacob’s earlier relationship with God.

questions.question: What does the repeated instruction to “lift up thine eyes” emphasize?
answers: The angel wanted Jacob to close his eyes
The event happened during the day, not in a dream
Jacob was to observe the vision carefully and understand its meaning
questions.explanation: The repetition highlights Jacob’s attention to the vision and its significance.

paragraphs.title: Rachel and Leah agree to leave

easy.question: Who spoke to Jacob in these verses?
answers: Rachel and Leah
Rebekah and Rachel
Leah and Zilpah
easy.explanation: Rachel and Leah answered Jacob.

easy.question: What did Jacob place his sons and wives upon?
answers: Horses
Camels
Carts
easy.explanation: Jacob placed them upon camels.

easy.question: Where did Jacob intend to go?
answers: Egypt
Haran
To Isaac his father in Canaan
easy.explanation: Jacob set out to go to Isaac his father in the land of Canaan.

medium.question: Why did Rachel and Leah say they had no portion or inheritance in their father’s house?
answers: Their father treated them as strangers, sold them, and consumed their money
Their father would not let them leave
They did not want any family property
medium.explanation: They said Laban had treated them as strangers, sold them, and used up their money.

medium.question: What did Jacob do after Rachel and Leah agreed with him?
answers: He went alone to Isaac
He rose, took his family, and led away his property
He stayed with Laban for more years
medium.explanation: Jacob rose and carried away his wives, sons, flock, and possessions.

medium.question: In “Are we not counted of him strangers?” what does “strangers” mean?
answers: Rich
Wise
Foreigners or outsiders
medium.explanation: Rachel and Leah felt that Laban treated them as outsiders rather than as beloved daughters.

challenge.question: What did Rachel and Leah claim about Jacob’s wealth?
answers: The wealth God took from their father belonged to them and their children
All the wealth belonged only to Laban
The wealth had to remain in Padan-aram
challenge.explanation: They said that the wealth God had taken from their father belonged to them and their children.

challenge.question: What sequence of events is described?
answers: Jacob reached Isaac and only afterward spoke with his wives
Rachel and Leah agreed, and Jacob left with his family and property toward Canaan
Laban gave Jacob everything, and Jacob stayed with him
challenge.explanation: Rachel and Leah agreed, after which Jacob left with his family and possessions.

challenge.question: What do the words “whatsoever God hath said unto thee, do” show?
answers: Rachel and Leah opposed leaving their father’s house
Jacob acted only because he feared Laban
Rachel and Leah supported Jacob’s obedience to God
challenge.explanation: They encouraged Jacob to do everything God had commanded him.

questions.question: What did Rachel and Leah claim about Jacob’s wealth?
answers: The wealth God took from their father belonged to them and their children
All the wealth belonged only to Laban
The wealth had to remain in Padan-aram
questions.explanation: They said that the wealth God had taken from their father belonged to them and their children.

questions.question: What sequence of events is described?
answers: Jacob reached Isaac and only afterward spoke with his wives
Rachel and Leah agreed, and Jacob left with his family and property toward Canaan
Laban gave Jacob everything, and Jacob stayed with him
questions.explanation: Rachel and Leah agreed, after which Jacob left with his family and possessions.

questions.question: What do the words “whatsoever God hath said unto thee, do” show?
answers: Rachel and Leah opposed leaving their father’s house
Jacob acted only because he feared Laban
Rachel and Leah supported Jacob’s obedience to God
questions.explanation: They encouraged Jacob to do everything God had commanded him.

easy.question: What did Laban go to do?
answers: Shear his sheep
Cross the river
Build a house
easy.explanation: Laban went to shear his sheep.

easy.question: What did Rachel steal from her father?
answers: The flock
The household images
His tent
easy.explanation: Rachel stole her father’s household images.

easy.question: Toward what did Jacob set his face?
answers: Egypt
Laban’s house
Mount Gilead
easy.explanation: Jacob set his face toward Mount Gilead.

medium.question: Why did Jacob not tell Laban that he was leaving?
answers: So he could leave secretly
Because he could not speak
Because Laban had already left
medium.explanation: Jacob did not tell Laban, so he departed secretly.

medium.question: What was the correct order of events?
answers: Jacob crossed the river, then Rachel stole the images
Laban went to shear, Rachel stole the images, and Jacob fled
Jacob reached Gilead, and then Laban went to shear
medium.explanation: Laban went to shear his sheep, Rachel stole the images, and Jacob fled.

medium.question: In “he told him not that he fled,” what does “not” indicate?
answers: Jacob left without telling Laban
Jacob left because of Laban
Jacob left after Laban
medium.explanation: Jacob fled without informing Laban.

challenge.question: What does “Jacob stole away unawares to Laban” mean here?
answers: Jacob hid his departure from Laban
Jacob took Laban into his house
Jacob stole an object from Laban
challenge.explanation: The phrase is explained by Jacob’s not telling Laban that he was fleeing.

challenge.question: What detail explains how Jacob could leave before Laban noticed?
answers: Jacob had already reached Gilead
Laban was busy shearing his sheep
Rachel told Laban about the departure
challenge.explanation: Laban was occupied with shearing, giving Jacob an opportunity to leave secretly.

challenge.question: What can be inferred from “all that he had”?
answers: Jacob fled alone
Jacob took only the household images
Jacob left with all his possessions
challenge.explanation: Jacob took his family, livestock, and everything he owned.

questions.question: What does “Jacob stole away unawares to Laban” mean here?
answers: Jacob hid his departure from Laban
Jacob took Laban into his house
Jacob stole an object from Laban
questions.explanation: Jacob did not tell Laban that he was fleeing.

questions.question: What detail explains how Jacob could leave before Laban noticed?
answers: Jacob had already reached Gilead
Laban was busy shearing his sheep
Rachel told Laban about the departure
questions.explanation: Laban was occupied with shearing, giving Jacob an opportunity to leave secretly.

questions.question: What can be inferred from “all that he had”?
answers: Jacob fled alone
Jacob took only the household images
Jacob left with all his possessions
questions.explanation: Jacob took his family, livestock, and everything he owned.

paragraphs.title: Laban pursues Jacob and receives a warning in a dream

easy.question: When did Laban learn that Jacob had fled?
answers: On the third day
On the first day
On the seventh day
easy.explanation: Laban was told on the third day that Jacob had fled.

easy.question: Who went with Laban to pursue Jacob?
answers: His sons
His brothers
His shepherds
easy.explanation: Laban took his brothers with him.

easy.question: Where did God warn Laban?
answers: At Jacob’s house
At Mount Gilead
In a dream by night
easy.explanation: God came to Laban in a dream by night.

medium.question: Why did Laban pursue Jacob?
answers: He learned that Jacob had fled
Jacob asked him to come
Laban’s brothers invited him
medium.explanation: Laban heard that Jacob had fled and pursued him.

medium.question: In “they overtook him,” what does “overtook” mean?
answers: Blessed him
Caught up with him
Hid from him
medium.explanation: After pursuing Jacob for seven days, Laban caught up with him.

medium.question: What is the correct order of events?
answers: Laban dreamed, learned of the flight, and then pursued Jacob
Jacob reached Gilead, and then Laban heard of his flight
Laban learned of the flight, pursued Jacob for seven days, and was then warned in a dream
medium.explanation: Laban first heard of the flight, then pursued Jacob, and God warned him after he caught up.

challenge.question: What can be inferred from Laban learning of Jacob’s flight only on the third day?
answers: Jacob had a head start before Laban began pursuing him
Laban pursued Jacob for only three days
Jacob waited three days for Laban
challenge.explanation: Jacob had already been traveling before Laban learned of his departure.

challenge.question: Why was Laban the one warned in the dream?
answers: He was far from his family
He was pursuing Jacob and might harm him
Jacob asked him for advice
challenge.explanation: Because Laban was pursuing Jacob, he needed to be warned not to harm him.

challenge.question: What does “either good or bad” mean in God’s warning?
answers: Laban could speak only about good things
Laban had to speak politely
Laban was not to speak to Jacob at all
challenge.explanation: The phrase includes both extremes and means that Laban was not to confront Jacob in any way.

questions.question: What can be inferred from Laban learning of Jacob’s flight only on the third day?
answers: Jacob had a head start before Laban began pursuing him
Laban pursued Jacob for only three days
Jacob waited three days for Laban
questions.explanation: Jacob had already been traveling before Laban learned of his departure.

questions.question: Why was Laban the one warned in the dream?
answers: He was far from his family
He was pursuing Jacob and might harm him
Jacob asked him for advice
questions.explanation: Because Laban was pursuing Jacob, he needed to be warned not to harm him.

questions.question: What does “either good or bad” mean in God’s warning?
answers: Laban could speak only about good things
Laban had to speak politely
Laban was not to speak to Jacob at all
questions.explanation: The phrase means that Laban was not to confront Jacob in any way.

easy.question: Who caught up with Jacob?
answers: Laban
Isaac
Esau
easy.explanation: Laban caught up with Jacob.

easy.question: Where had Jacob pitched his tent?
answers: In the valley
On the mountain
In the city
easy.explanation: Jacob had pitched his tent on the mountain.

easy.question: What instruments did Laban say he would have used to send Jacob away?
answers: Trumpet and flute
Dance and ram’s horn
Tambrel and harp
easy.explanation: Laban said he would have sent Jacob away with a tambrel and harp.

medium.question: Why did Laban say he was hurt that Jacob left secretly?
answers: He was not given a chance to say farewell joyfully to his daughters
Jacob took all his flock
Jacob did not want to live on the mountain
medium.explanation: Laban claimed that he would have sent Jacob away joyfully and said farewell to his daughters.

medium.question: In “Why didst thou flee away secretly,” what does “secretly” mean?
answers: Prepared to celebrate
Acted without telling anyone
Settled on the mountain
medium.explanation: Laban accused Jacob of hiding his departure and leaving without informing him.

medium.question: What sequence of events is described?
answers: Laban warned Jacob, Jacob fled, and Laban said farewell
Jacob said farewell joyfully, Laban warned him, and Jacob fled
Jacob fled, Laban caught up with him, and God warned Laban
medium.explanation: Jacob left, Laban caught up with him, and God had warned Laban before he confronted Jacob.

challenge.question: Why did Laban say he could harm Jacob but did not?
answers: God had warned him not to speak to Jacob for good or bad
Jacob apologized
Laban forgot why he pursued him
challenge.explanation: Laban admitted that the God of Jacob’s father had restrained him.

challenge.question: What did Laban mean by “thou hast stolen away from me”?
answers: Jacob took Laban into his house
Jacob left secretly and hid his intention
Jacob literally stole Laban’s heart
challenge.explanation: Laban complained that Jacob had hidden his departure and prevented a farewell.

challenge.question: What contrast appears between “captives taken with the sword” and Laban’s claim that he would have sent Jacob away joyfully?
answers: Laban thought his daughters were going to war
Laban intended his daughters to remain home
Laban described their sudden departure as forced, while claiming he would otherwise have parted joyfully
challenge.explanation: Laban portrayed their sudden departure as captivity while claiming he would have said goodbye happily.

questions.question: Why did Laban say he could harm Jacob but did not?
answers: God had warned him not to speak to Jacob for good or bad
Jacob apologized
Laban forgot why he pursued him
questions.explanation: Laban admitted that God had restrained him.

questions.question: What did Laban mean by “thou hast stolen away from me”?
answers: Jacob took Laban into his house
Jacob left secretly and hid his intention
Jacob literally stole Laban’s heart
questions.explanation: Laban complained that Jacob had hidden his departure and prevented a farewell.

questions.question: What contrast appears between “captives taken with the sword” and Laban’s claim that he would have sent Jacob away joyfully?
answers: Laban thought his daughters were going to war
Laban intended his daughters to remain home
Laban described their sudden departure as forced, while claiming he would otherwise have parted joyfully
questions.explanation: Laban portrayed their sudden departure as captivity while claiming he would have said goodbye happily.

paragraphs.title: Jacob explains his flight and Laban searches for the images

easy.question: What was Jacob afraid of?
answers: That Laban would take his daughters from him
That Laban would take his flock
That Laban would drive him from the land
easy.explanation: Jacob feared that Laban would forcibly take his daughters from him.

easy.question: Who stole the household images?
answers: Leah
Rachel
One of the maidservants
easy.explanation: Rachel had stolen the household images.

easy.question: Where did Rachel put the images?
answers: In Leah’s tent
In a chest
In the camel’s furniture
easy.explanation: Rachel put the images in the camel’s furniture and sat on them.

medium.question: Why did Laban fail to find the images?
answers: Rachel hid them in the camel’s furniture and sat on them
Jacob moved them to Leah’s tent
Laban stopped searching before reaching Rachel’s tent
medium.explanation: Rachel hid the images beneath her and prevented Laban from seeing them.

medium.question: In what order did Laban search the tents?
answers: Rachel, Leah, Jacob, and the maidservants
Jacob, Leah, the maidservants, and Rachel
Leah, Rachel, Jacob, and the maidservants
medium.explanation: Laban searched Jacob’s tent, Leah’s tent, the maidservants’ tents, and finally Rachel’s tent.

medium.question: What were the household images?
answers: Tools
Traveling clothes
Household idols
medium.explanation: The images were household idols that Rachel had hidden.

challenge.question: What excuse did Rachel use so she would not rise before her father?
answers: She said she was experiencing the custom of women
She said she was asleep
She said she feared Jacob
challenge.explanation: Rachel said that the custom of women was upon her, preventing Laban from checking the camel’s furniture.

challenge.question: What was ironic about Jacob’s statement that whoever had the images should not live?
answers: Jacob said Laban had stolen them
Jacob unknowingly pronounced a severe punishment on Rachel, who had stolen them
Jacob knew Rachel was hiding them
challenge.explanation: Jacob did not know that Rachel had taken the images.

challenge.question: What does “Let it not displease my lord” mean?
answers: Do not look at me
Do not close your eyes
Do not be angry with me
challenge.explanation: Rachel was asking Laban not to be angry with her.

questions.question: What excuse did Rachel use so she would not rise before her father?
answers: She said she was experiencing the custom of women
She said she was asleep
She said she feared Jacob
questions.explanation: Rachel said that the custom of women was upon her, preventing Laban from checking the camel’s furniture.

questions.question: What was ironic about Jacob’s statement that whoever had the images should not live?
answers: Jacob said Laban had stolen them
Jacob unknowingly pronounced a severe punishment on Rachel, who had stolen them
Jacob knew Rachel was hiding them
questions.explanation: Jacob did not know that Rachel had taken the images.

questions.question: What does “Let it not displease my lord” mean?
answers: Do not look at me
Do not close your eyes
Do not be angry with me
questions.explanation: Rachel was asking Laban not to be angry with her.

paragraphs.title: Jacob rebukes Laban for his difficult years of service

easy.question: Why was Jacob angry and argued with Laban?
answers: Because Laban pursued him
Because Jacob lost all his flock
Because Isaac rebuked him
easy.explanation: Jacob was angry because Laban had pursued him.

easy.question: How many years in total had Jacob served Laban?
answers: Seven years
Twenty years
Fourteen years
easy.explanation: Jacob said he had been with Laban for twenty years.

easy.question: What weather conditions did Jacob endure?
answers: Rain by day and snow by night
Wind by day and heat by night
Heat or drought by day and frost by night
easy.explanation: Jacob described suffering from heat or drought during the day and frost at night.

medium.question: What did Jacob mean by saying that without God Laban would have sent him away empty?
answers: God protected him from leaving without wages or property
Laban had given him everything
Jacob had never worked for Laban
medium.explanation: Jacob said that God’s protection kept Laban from sending him away without compensation.

medium.question: What is an animal “torn of beasts”?
answers: An animal that was born
An animal attacked or killed by a wild animal
An animal sold in the market
medium.explanation: Jacob refers to an animal injured or killed by another beast, for which Laban required payment.

medium.question: How did Jacob divide his twenty years of service?
answers: Ten years for the daughters and ten for the flock
Seven years for the daughters and thirteen for the flock
Fourteen years for the daughters and six for the flock
medium.explanation: Jacob served fourteen years for Laban’s two daughters and six years for the flock.

challenge.question: What did Jacob emphasize by saying God had seen his affliction and the labor of his hands?
answers: God saw his suffering and work and rebuked Laban
Laban saw his work and praised him
Jacob had stopped working the previous night
challenge.explanation: Jacob claimed that God had witnessed his hardship and intervened against Laban.

challenge.question: Who is meant by “the fear of Isaac”?
answers: Isaac’s fear of Jacob
God, whom Isaac revered
Laban’s fear of Isaac
challenge.explanation: “The fear of Isaac” is a title for God, whom Isaac feared and worshiped.

challenge.question: What does “thou hast changed my wages ten times” mean?
answers: Laban always paid Jacob in the same way
Jacob changed Laban’s wages
Laban changed the wage terms repeatedly
challenge.explanation: Laban repeatedly altered the terms of Jacob’s wages.

questions.question: What did Jacob emphasize by saying God had seen his affliction and the labor of his hands?
answers: God saw his suffering and work and rebuked Laban
Laban saw his work and praised him
Jacob had stopped working the previous night
questions.explanation: Jacob claimed that God had witnessed his hardship and intervened against Laban.

questions.question: Who is meant by “the fear of Isaac”?
answers: Isaac’s fear of Jacob
God, whom Isaac revered
Laban’s fear of Isaac
questions.explanation: “The fear of Isaac” is a title for God.

questions.question: What does “thou hast changed my wages ten times” mean?
answers: Laban always paid Jacob in the same way
Jacob changed Laban’s wages
Laban changed the wage terms repeatedly
questions.explanation: Laban repeatedly altered the terms of Jacob’s wages.

paragraphs.title: Laban claims everything belongs to him and proposes a covenant

easy.question: Who answered Jacob?
answers: Laban
Esau
Isaac
easy.explanation: Laban answered Jacob.

easy.question: What did Laban propose?
answers: Going to war
Making a covenant
Returning to Haran
easy.explanation: Laban proposed that they make a covenant.

easy.question: What was the covenant meant to be?
answers: A gift to Jacob
A way to divide the flock
A witness between Laban and Jacob
easy.explanation: Laban said the covenant would be a witness between them.

medium.question: What does Laban’s statement that the daughters, children, flock, and everything Jacob saw were his show?
answers: Laban claimed that everything belonged to him or was connected to him
Laban wanted to leave everything to Jacob
